name: Astragalus
short: In kidney disease trials (many of injected astragalus) adverse events were similar to control, but many trials did not report them and quality was low. May interact with drugs such as digoxin.
text: Safety data from trials are limited. In a systematic review of 22 trials (1323 participants) of astragalus for chronic kidney disease, six trials reported that no adverse effects were observed and the other 16 did not report on adverse effects, and overall study quality was low. In a meta-analysis of 66 trials (4785 participants) of astragalus preparations added to conventional treatment for diabetic kidney disease (the pooled analyses in the abstract cover up to 32 trials of astragalus injection and four of oral preparations), the adverse-events profile was similar between the astragalus and control groups; the authors rated the evidence as low quality and called for further trials of long-term safety, especially of the oral form. For interactions, a review of metabolic studies says astragalus root and its main components affect drug-metabolising enzymes and transporters (notably CYP2C9, CYP3A4, UGT1A6 and P-gp) and may contribute to herb-drug interactions when taken with drugs handled by them, such as tolbutamide, midazolam and digoxin; the review notes that studies disagree on some of these effects, such as that on CYP3A4, and the abstract does not say whether any interaction has been confirmed in patients.
